profiles.name: CRANK
profiles.profile: This is the kind of profile that makes you squint at the numbers and then blame the driver in a whisper. CRANK keeps finding ways to hang around the top of the NET board even when the tee game is actively setting fire to the round. The rescue act is real: when the approach is sideways, the short game shows up with a shovel and a cigarette. It’s messy, volatile golf, but it’s not random. When he’s not nuking himself off the property line, he can absolutely survive on touch and nerve.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.profile: MattF is playing the kind of golf that makes everybody else feel like they accidentally showed up for a different format. The ball-striking ceiling is stupid, and when the irons are cooking he looks like a guy who can just print birdies and walk away without paying attention. The catch is that the floor isn’t exactly holy ground: there are enough chunky patches and messy moments to keep the scorecard from getting too smug. Basically, this is elite upside with a little chaos tax baked in. A dangerous combo, because it can beat you before you’ve even found your glove.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.profile: Dan94 keeps showing up like a guy who can solve a golf course by bullying it into submission. The tee ball is the headline, but the whole bag is usually loud enough to back it up, which is why the gross file keeps looking nasty for everybody else. The weird part is that the ball can be violent without being tidy, so the round occasionally gets sprinkled with dumb stress that shouldn’t exist for someone hitting it this hard. Still, the repeatable identity is obvious: aggressive golf, huge ceiling, and enough complete-hole domination to make the rest of the room look like they’re working retail.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.profile: KeithK75 is the guy most likely to make a course look stupid for no good reason other than he showed up feeling mean. The irons are the backbone here, and when those are in gear the rest of the round tends to stop mattering. He’s got enough short-game and putting support to turn good ball-striking into actual damage, which is why the file keeps reading like a legitimate threat instead of a one-trick bomber. There’s some volatility in the mix, sure, but the identity is not subtle: hit it close, make some shit, leave the rest of the field staring at the divot.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.tagline: ONE GOOD SWING, TWO BAD MEMES
profiles.profile: BigTime is the classic case of a player who can still make a round look expensive even when the driver isn’t the problem. The long game has enough juice to keep him alive, but the scoring keeps leaking through the soft spots, especially when the short game starts acting like it forgot the assignment. There’s a real tendency for the round to get bogged down in extra putts and extra damage, which is a brutal hobby in this league. The upside is there, but the identity is pretty clear: if the touch game doesn’t cooperate, the whole operation gets mugged in broad daylight.

profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.profile: HamSammich is the guy whose rounds often feel like a bar fight between a decent putter and everything else. The putter can keep him from completely face-planting, but the rest of the bag has a bad habit of introducing chaos at the worst possible time. The short game gets weird, the big numbers sneak in, and suddenly the scorecard looks like it had a rough childhood. There’s enough pop to avoid total disaster, but the profile lives in the land of damage control. Not pretty, not clean, and somehow still capable of hanging around when the putter decides to act like a grown-up.
